W2 (empirical), after E021. Tip is E017: 6.548 s, 0.7537, only ~0.07 pp above the 0.753 bar.

Measured chain: E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 -0.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E015 CUDA graphs 0.7574/6.58. E016 wd/2 0.7607/6.58. E017 break-free 0.7537/6.548. E018 24/32 only 0.7502/5.99. E019 rerun of E016 code 0.7541/6.54. E020 -1 epoch 0.7528/5.86. E021 group 2 at 320: 0.7530/6.04.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: ~0.1 pp and ~5% time per 0.5 epoch (E020, E008). Roughly linear and cheap.
2. EMA/Lookahead gives +0.97 pp for +0.06 s (E005). Muon gives +0.66 pp for +0.35 s (E006).
3. Time tracks FLOPs and pixel count. Narrowing group 2 to 320 (E021) cut 7.8% of time for -0.08 pp vs E016 (-0.3 pp if E019 is taken as the baseline). That is a cheap trade, in the same range as the epoch dial. Width 576->512 (E010) cut 4.8% for -0.25 pp. Resolution cuts (E011, E018) are the costliest in accuracy per unit of time.
4. wd, LS, Muon lr and LR floor are flat within noise. E016's 0.7607 was noise (E019 got 0.7541 on the same code, so the true mean is ~0.754).
5. CUDA graphs and break removal give ~1% each. The run is compute-bound.
6. Noise: a rerun of identical code is bit-identical, but a math-identical edit reshuffles the 3-seed mean by ±0.3-0.4 pp. Time noise is ~0.5%.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and E016, and was too pessimistic on the time of E011, E020 and E021. I over-predicted E018. Lesson: time effects are predictable, but accuracy differences below 0.4 pp are unresolvable.

Unsure: whether the tip's true mean clears 0.75 on 40 seeds, and whether any free accuracy gain exists. Any further trim lands near 0.752-0.753, so the 0.753 bar becomes a coin flip.

forecasts.reason: wd effects measured flat; E016 gain was noise (E019). Expect a reshuffle around 0.754, not +0.2 pp.
Dropping a conv cuts ~7% of time but costs ~0.3-0.4 pp, so it falls below 0.75. The accuracy loss is likely above the 0.4 pp limit in the hypothesis.
A 20 px phase over 15% of steps saves ~3-4% of time and likely loses ~0.15 pp, which is within noise. The hypothesis wants at least 4% time saved and a loss of at most 0.25 pp.

cruxes: What is the true 40-seed mean accuracy of the tip? E019 and E012 suggest ~0.754, and the 0.753 bar is then a coin flip for any trim.
Does narrowing group 2 to 320 (E021: -7.8% time, ~-0.1 to -0.3 pp) combined with EMA/wd changes give a net gain that still clears 0.753?
Is the remaining time compute-bound, so that only FLOP cuts help? That decides whether architecture or epoch trims beat the other levers.
